audit.title: Developer Responsibilities: Market Integrity and Application Code Risks

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong openings: Market Integrity vs Application Code risks are defined up front, and "The **market status flag** included in price reports is the authoritative signal" is a clean liftable claim. Weak spot: the top of the page opens with product marketing prose before stating what the page is *for*.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good: 10 headings, 1 H1, no level skips, 0 sections over 600 words (max 381), 22 bullets. Weakness: 0 tables — the asset-type → trading-window → 24/7 mapping is prime table material currently buried in prose bullets.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only the "15-minute delay" for UK ETFs is a hard number; FX pairs, market-hours windows, latency ranges, and retry/backoff parameters are all described qualitatively. Vague quantifiers (`some`, `most`, `significant`, `substantial`) stand in for figures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Adequate: 13 links, good internal cross-links to architecture/best-practices, plus the education-hub manipulation article. Zero links to primary/canonical spec sources (e.g., the Verifier contract reference or report-schema definition).

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. Bolded, self-contained definitions of both risk classes and the authoritative-signal statement are verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak and measurable: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read — but nothing was served.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 fenced blocks. This is largely a prose page, so low expectation, but it references `observationsTimestamp`, SDK config, and retry-with-backoff without a single inline snippet showing the correct flag check.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers market hours, DEX assets, new tokens, custom streams, contingency logic. Missing symptom-phrased entry points (e.g., "why is my equity stream stale outside market hours") and any FAQ/troubleshooting framing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; "Chainlink Data Streams" is used consistently, prose is unambiguous. Mild repetition of "solely responsible" but not harmful.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured risk-disclosure and responsibilities page for Chainlink Data Streams, and its strongest GEO asset is a clear, repeatedly-stated canonical rule: use the **market status flag**, not `observationsTimestamp`, to determine stream availability. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability — no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dated freshness signals were served — compounded by thin quantitative specifics (5 numerals in ~1,950 words, none with units) that leave engines little to lift. The honest verdict: good prose that reads as a policy document, but under-instrumented for retrieval and under-specified for confident synthesis; it will lose retrieval on symptom-phrased queries it actually answers.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about` (Chainlink Data Streams), and a self-referencing `canonical`; render a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and entity metadata raise parse-trust and E-E-A-T; measurably absent here.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased headings / a short FAQ
recommendations.where: new H3s under Market hours and a closing FAQ
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("Market hours", "DEX-based Assets"), not query-shaped.
recommendations.change: Add sections like "Why is my equity/ETF stream returning a stale or unchanged price?" and "How do I tell if a market is open — timestamp vs market status flag?" answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom; the page already contains these answers but won't be retrieved for the questions users actually type.

recommendations.title: Convert the asset-type / trading-window bullets into a comparison table
recommendations.issue: equity/ETF, Forex, UK ETF, DEX rules are prose bullets; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: Add a table: Asset class | Trading window | 24/7? | Known delay | Use market status flag?. Put the 15-min UK ETF delay in a cell.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract per-asset reasons and build justified, quotable answers.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics where currently qualitative
recommendations.issue: "most traditional markets do not trade 24/7", retry "with exponential backoff" — no numbers.
recommendations.change: Name the supported FX majors explicitly, state representative market-hours windows (with timezone), and give a concrete backoff example (e.g., base delay, max retries) linked to the retry-guidance anchor.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes; the page is at 3 numerals/1k words.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal inline snippet showing the market-status-flag check
recommendations.where: after "market status flag ... is the authoritative signal"
recommendations.issue: the canonical rule is stated but never shown in code; agents may fall back to `observationsTimestamp`.
recommendations.change: Add a short, language-tagged snippet reading the market-status field and explicitly commenting the timestamp path as the wrong approach.
recommendations.why: Naming the tempting-wrong pattern (`observationsTimestamp`) as a Don't in runnable form defends against parametric fallback to timestamp-based logic.

recommendations.title: Link to primary/canonical sources
recommendations.issue: 0 links to primary sources; Verifier Contract and report schema are named but unlinked.
recommendations.change: Inline-link the Verifier Contract reference and the price-report schema definition at first mention.
recommendations.why: Primary-source links raise citation rate and let engines attribute the `observationsTimestamp` / market-status-flag claims.

recommendations.title: Tighten the marketing lede into an answer-first opener
recommendations.issue: opens with "Chainlink Data Streams provide access to high-frequency market data backed by decentralized, fault-tolerant..."
recommendations.change: Lead with one sentence stating what the page defines: "Developers integrating Chainlink Data Streams bear two responsibility classes — market integrity risk and application code risk — defined below."
recommendations.why: A self-contained first sentence chunks cleanly and answers the page's implied question.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers (`some`, `most`, `significant`, `substantial`) used where numbers would serve — flagged, not double-penalized.
Mild repetition of "solely responsible for" across sections; acceptable in a legal-risk context but adds diffuse prose.
No tables despite tabular content (asset/market-hours mapping) — scannability opportunity, not a hard error.
offPageNotes: Head metadata was not captured by the harness — pass raw `<head>` so JSON-LD/canonical/date signals can be confirmed rather than inferred absent.
Page references `/llms.txt`; ensure this file lists this URL so agents discover it in the site index.
Freshness cadence is a site-level concern — a visible review date on risk-disclosure pages matters more than on tutorials for trust signals.
